full_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / precise-object redesign. Create one standalone RHYTHM PIVOT cultivation-array component by developing the same physical material language as the referenced artifacts. Reference Image 1 (the selected B array plate) is the HIGHEST art-style authority; Reference Image 2 (the finished eye component) confirms the exact dark ink contour, simplified gray-brown copper / gray-celadon jade planes, narrow ivory-white bevel highlights and restrained dry-brush watercolor texture. Borrow the painting language, NOT the eye's square shape or its four side tabs. No realistic polished metal or photoreal gears.

Design a NEW distinct intact horizontal RHYTHM PIVOT, a ONE-PIECE low ancient copper-and-jade instrument. True HORIZONTAL 2:1 canvas AND broad physical silhouette: width twice height, full piece occupies about 88-92% of both canvas dimensions, clean small transparent safety margin. It must visibly occupy two cells, never a small square jewel lost in a wide canvas. The component remains flat and shallow.

Anatomy: on the LEFT half, a pair of flat gray-celadon JADE REED LEAVES lies lengthwise within a shallow copper seat. These are two low bowed/slightly curved thin jade strips, secured at one end and lying parallel to the top surface, NOT upright springs and NOT loose stones. On the RIGHT half, a low OPEN COPPER REGULATING COLLAR / PRESSURE LEAF works around a small pale-jade contact bed, its partial stepped arc or C-shaped retaining plate clearly OPEN, not a complete round clock face. The jade reed pair and right pressure collar are physically connected by one subdued shallow copper base and small structural bridges, forming a substantial clean horizontal silhouette with different mechanisms on the two halves. Precise but broadly hand-painted ancient craft, not a fine realistic clock movement. Keep it different from a counting mechanism or jade tally sliding ruler: no ruler, sliding abacus rail, rows of bead counters or tally marks.

EXACTLY TWO SIGNAL SOCKETS with small CINNABAR-RED inset cores: (1) one INPUT socket at the LEFT/WEST SIDE MIDPOINT of the LEFT half, opening LEFT; (2) one OUTPUT socket at the TOP/NORTH SIDE MIDPOINT of the RIGHT half, opening UP, at approximately x=75% across the complete two-cell footprint. Both openings are simple shaped copper notches with short cinnabar cores, completely inside the safe image border. No outward line, pipe, arrow or lead. The ENTIRE RIGHT/EAST edge and BOTTOM/SOUTH edge stay closed, no sockets or misleading contact tabs. No energy/gold socket, no third port. Do not reuse four-direction socket framing from the reference eye.

STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC 90-DEGREE TOP-DOWN VIEW: see flat top faces, no isometric tilt, no front-facing/side walls, no raised vertical reeds. Dark ink outlines, a few clear painted light and shadow planes and narrow ivory highlights give restrained physical depth. Palette and brushwork must look as if this belonged to the selected B plate and the eye in the references. Do not draw the plate underneath.

Genuine transparent alpha outside the whole component and any real open cutout. No paper/background card, chess grid, floor or exterior shadow, checkerboard background, text, numerals, runes, labels, UI, clock face, clock numbers, hands of a clock, gears, hourglass, modern electronics, chip package, shield, jewel pendant, emitted effect, magic glow, external wires or extra parts. The idea is a rhythm-regulating physical jade-reed assembly, not a timekeeping icon. It only regulates the frequency of incoming signals and does not depict a new signal source or a chosen time interval.
